goal: Activate the canonical PostgreSQL gear Resolver behind a structured resolve endpoint, publish backend-owned Intent authoring revisions, and add a canonical profile mode that re-resolves Intent while preserving the legacy profile contract.
userValue: The equipment workbench can ask the server for current legality, deterministic attributes, set state, evidence and profile readiness instead of trusting client-computed final facts, while old clients continue to work.
nonGoals: No frontend page cutover in Slice 3A
No change to the legacy profile response for bodies without selectionIntent
No change to the legacy gear stats response or execution flavor
No database migration, write, sync, backfill, cleanup, job, Worker, service or timer
No formal Phase 4 Active Season Manifest or release registry
No public baseline, recommendation, DPS comparison or BiS behavior
No dependency installation or unapproved local download

mustChange: one shared backend resolver authoring context derived from the Phase 2 revision row
one runtime orchestration module over the existing store, Resolver, Result Envelope and profile facade
focused store, orchestration, route, compatibility and live-query tests
Strict evidence, owner map, verification matrix, runbook and roadmap state
mustNotChange: pure Resolver and Evidence Ledger ownership
legacy profile response for old request bodies
public observed-only and baseline-empty template semantics
evidenceRequired: TDD proof for resolver context, orchestration and route HTTP mapping
one read-only revision query for public authoring context and unchanged selected-context query budget
client final-fact rejection and canonical profile re-resolve proof
legacy profile and gear stats compatibility characterization
backend and full verification profiles plus local CR
candidate exact identity, 40-spec live resolve, profile, SLO, negative HTTP, public, timer, log and rollback evidence

engineeringHealth.reason: Slice 3A adds one injectable orchestration boundary and one additive resolver context; it reuses all Phase 2 pure/domain/store owners and does not add another database or rule source.

acceptanceEvidence: Python compile, static query-boundary inspection and git diff --check
candidate live 40-spec resolve/profile, negative HTTP, SLO/cache, legacy/public/timer/log and rollback proof

decisionLog.decision: Use three Phase 3 strangler Slices: backend API, dormant frontend transport/state, then active page cutover.
Publish additive resolverContext from the same transitional revision authority as the loader; formalActiveManifest remains false until Phase 4.
Canonical profile requests contain selectionIntent and are re-resolved; legacy bodies retain their current response shape.
409 preserves choices and may rebase revisions once; 503 never becomes generic frontend fallback or stale SimC execution.
